business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Precision Steel Injection Molding of Color Snap-Fit Plastic Kits

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland maintains over 90 active Bilateral Investment Treaties; the applicable investor-protection treaty is determined by the ultimate beneficial owner's nationality (e.g., Swiss-China BIT, in force 2020).
Double Taxation Agreements (DTAAs) framework including the Swiss-US DTAA (2011) and Swiss-Japan DTAA (1971, amended 2019) govern withholding and repatriation planning.
EFTA Convention (2001) and EFTA-third-country trade agreements (e.g., EFTA-Korea FTA of 2006) cover tariffs applicable to manufactured games, toys, and plastic model kits.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 627a (beneficial-owner declaration in the registration application); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) Arts. 2, 7 and 16; Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (SR 221.411.1); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Arts. 305bis and 305ter; FINMA Circular 2024/01 on AML/CFT conduct.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The UBO's home-country competent authority (consular or police issuance office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the home country is a 1961 Convention state; otherwise Consular Legalization through the competent Swiss representation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed and dated beneficial-owner declaration (beneficial-owner identification schema per Art. 627a CO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBO and incorporators, notarially attested where the foreign UBO is located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization followed by Swiss notarial confirmation of signatures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or corporate excerpt of any corporate shareholder (direct corporate UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or chamber of commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (capped at 90 days for this filing)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of lawful source of funds for the CHF 100,000 share-capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign bank letters or notarially confirmed bank certification; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (Statuts/Gesellschaftsstatuten) including registered office, capital schedule and director identity provisions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Swiss notarial deed; no apostille required for the Swiss Commercial Register (apostille only if the deed is exported abroad)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, incorporators, signatories and UBOs must be screened against the UN Security Council sanctions list, the Swiss SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) embargo and sanctions ordinance, and EU restrictive measures adopted by Switzerland. Foreign PEPs per AMLA Art. 2 trigger enhanced due diligence, requiring documented source of wealth and source of funds prior to incorporation. As the target payment rails include SWIFT and PayPal, parallel OFAC SDN screening is recommended in the compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office; official publication via the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The firm must be expressed in at least one official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) in Latin script and must include the legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'Société Anonyme', 'Società per Azioni' or the accepted abbreviation ('AG'/'SA'). Additional English-language names are admitted where no misleading effect arises; foreign-script brand elements must be transliterated into Latin characters.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss/Schweiz/Suisse/Svizzera (requires Federal Council authorization and substantial local presence)
Group/Holding (only where group substance and ownership structure qualify)
Anime/Gundam/Pokemon or third-party trademarks (intellectual-property objections are a commercial-register rejection ground)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name clearance (negative attestation) from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office remains valid through the 90-day incorporation process; if registration is not completed within that window, a renewed name-verification application is required. A rejection is served with a written statement of reasons and may be appealed in writing within 30 days to the cantonal supervisory authority over the commercial register; further appeal lies to the Cantonal Administrative Court and finally to the Federal Supreme Court (Art. 82 et seq. Federal Administrative Procedure Act). Trademark disputes proceed separately in civil litigation before the cantonal commercial courts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual-office addresses are not admissible as the sole seat of an Aktiengesellschaft: Art. 625 CO requires the registered office to correspond to the place of actual administration. Third-party managed offices and corporate-service-provider premises are accepted only when directors genuinely exercise management and maintain corporate records there. For a manufacturing entity, both the factory premises and the registered office must demonstrate real operational substance within Switzerland.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced inspection: Commercial Register Office — low (≈10%) during post-incorporation monitoring; local tax and AHV/AVS social-insurance authorities — moderate (≈25%) for a manufacturing start-up in the first 36 months; factory-premises verification is a standard condition for zoning and VAT registration rather than a compliance inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Firm-name preliminary clearance and negative attestation (Zefix/commercial register name check)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee tariff under the Commercial Register Ordinance (approx. CHF 150).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association, beneficial-owner declaration and capital-payment confirmation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff benchmark (approx. CHF 2,500; canton-specific scale).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Register entry fee and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB) publication charge
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and SHAB
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (approx. CHF 800–900 including gazette publication).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance bundle — UBO piercing, PEP/sanctions screening and source-of-capital file
Apostille/consular legalization of three certified origin documents (UBO ID, UBO declaration, corporate good-standing certificate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal apostille authority and/or Swiss consulate for non-Convention jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fee (approx. CHF 20–40 per document).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage-1 legal advisory — name candidacy review, corporate-governance structure, AML documentation and incorporation supervision
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (approx. CHF 4,000) under Swiss Lawyers' Fee Regulation norms.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), Arts. 620-763 governing the Aktiengesellschaft / Stock Corporation; specifically Arts. 629-635 (mandatory articles and public notarization), Arts. 632-633 (minimum capital and payment rules), Art. 640 (registered shares), and Art. 695 (Commercial Register application); supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411), Arts. 68-69.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), Switzerland; federal electronic filing through the eGRC / EasyGov.swiss portal; nationwide publication by the Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Anmeldung zur Eintragung in das Handelsregister (Application for Registration in the Commercial Register, Form of the HRegV Annex for stock companies) executed by the notary and filed electronically with the Handelsregisteramt Zug.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV/FTA) – competent for Swiss federal direct taxes, withholding tax, stamp duties and VAT; e-portal: www.estv.admin.ch with the SaaS e-service for VAT registration and returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CH_AG obtains its statutory UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) automatically from the Cantonal Commercial Register entry. For VAT: file FTA registration questionnaire, current official register extract, articles of association and proof of place of management within 30 days of exceeding the CHF 100,000 worldwide turnover threshold; the FTA issues the MWST/TVA/IVA VAT identification number, which is the UID followed by the MWST/TVA/IVA suffix.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: The Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is a per-se corporation subject to federal, cantonal and municipal income tax on worldwide profits, with carve-outs for foreign permanent establishments, foreign real property and participation exemptions; passthrough treatment is not available for Swiss resident shareholders; export manufacturing income qualifies for the 0% VAT rate with full input VAT deduction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss VAT group election (Art. 15 VAT Act); option to tax exempt real estate supplies (Art. 21(3) VAT Act); cantonal holding, mixed company and principal-company tax status rulings; notional interest deduction election on excess Swiss equity of the AG; participation deduction election (Art. 70 DBG); hybrid mismatch elections reported under Art. 61a DBG; no US check-the-box election domestically, but an associated US parent may file check-the-box elections for solo entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer – MWST / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover for Swiss-established entities (Art. 10(1) VAT Act); non-established foreign suppliers register once Swiss taxable supplies exceed CHF 100,000 per year (Art. 10(3) VAT Act); voluntary taxation election is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping or digital invoice clearance is mandated in Switzerland. Domestic invoices must include a QR-bill payment slip (Swiss Payment Standards, ISO 20022) since 1 July 2020; PEPPOL and other B2B/B2G e-invoice formats are accepted voluntarily; FTA returns are filed via the SaaS e-portal; all invoice and export evidence must be retained electronically for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Switzerland are zero-rated under Art. 23(1) VAT Act when the exporter proves delivery to a foreign destination; services directly related to exported goods and services under Art. 23(2) also qualify; the CH_AG must demonstrate per consignment the foreign recipient, value chain and physical dispatch of the action-figure mecha model kits; dispatch into a bonded warehouse or export-only delivery is excluded from domestic Swiss VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrschein / export visa B) or EU/EFTA common transit document
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Switzerland
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment proof evidencing settlement of the export invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, missing or inconsistent export proof triggers reclassification of supplies at the 8.1% standard rate with statutory default interest, denial of input VAT deduction and retroactive deficiency assessments for up to 10 years; negligent evasion triggers a fine of up to 100% of the VAT evaded, intentional evasion a fine of up to 300% (Art. 99 VAT Act) and criminal penalties (Art. 101 VAT Act); false customs declarations are separately sanctionable under Art. 118 Customs Act. Swiss law imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline, so the 180-day term is enforced by banks and auditors as a documentary benchmark for export substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), acting together with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) in matters of monetary policy, international financial sanctions, and banking supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully liberalized cross-border capital and payments regime. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely convertible, and there are no general restrictions on current account payments, capital injections, dividend distributions, or repatriation of liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance from a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is not subject to exchange-control approval; the only practical hurdles are corporate-law solvency tests, statutory reserves, and the 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividend distributions unless reduced under an applicable double tax treaty or the Swiss participation exemption conditions are met. No prior central-bank authorization is required for inbound or outbound transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no mandatory surrender or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in any convertible currency, used directly for offshore working capital, or converted into CHF at the exporter's discretion. There is no statutory conversion ratio, no prescribed settlement window, and no SNB requirement to convert foreign currency balances. Swiss resident companies may need to comply only with statistical balance-of-payments reporting thresholds of the SNB for large direct investment or cross-border financial claims, not with any exchange-control liquidation obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Einzahlungskonto) for share capital deposit and Operational Account in CHF/EUR/USD
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with multi-currency treasury services
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account; suitable for SME manufacturing
Operational Account for domestic CHF clearing and retail collections

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-conditional. A Swiss AG may use a licensed foreign or Swiss-licensed fintech electronic-money institution (EMI) as a supplementary collections and treasury-optimization rail, but such an account cannot replace a Swiss banking relationship for statutory share-capital deposit, SIC/SNB CHF clearing, or documentary trade instruments. Offshore EMIs that are not licensed or passported into Switzerland create legal uncertainty under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act and may expose the company to reputational and sanctions-screening risks. Acceptable use is limited to low-value inbound customer collections, and the controlling compliance function must ensure every fintech account is covered by the company's tax and financial reporting perimeter.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a standard low-risk Swiss AG, a fully remote account opening is generally available if all directors and beneficial owners provide electronic identification under a FINMA-compliant digital onboarding process. However, most tier-1 Swiss banks reserve the right to require one physical interview or notarized signature verification when the beneficial owner is a non-resident, when the registered office is a virtual office, or when the onboarding jurisdiction is on the bank's higher-risk list. For this action-figure and plastic model-kit manufacturer, the expected compliance path is remote KYC with certified passports, a Swiss commercial-register extract, and a board resolution; physical attendance is recommended for the first treasury relationship to reduce friction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner tax residence or nationality in a jurisdiction with FATF or internal bank higher-risk classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports, proof of tax residence in Switzerland or a low-risk jurisdiction, CV and professional background, source-of-wealth statement supported by audited financial statements, bank reference letters, and a corporate structure chart evidencing the identity and footprint of every natural-person beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of physical or operational substance in Switzerland, including virtual registered office and no visible manufacturing footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a Swiss commercial or light-industrial registered office, Swiss payroll records or social-security registration for employees, a detailed business plan for high-precision steel injection molding, procurement contracts for steel and polymer resins, warehouse or fulfillment agreements, and photographs or facility documentation supporting physical substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or non-transparent source of initial share capital, particularly if funded by a third party or via aggregating payment platforms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution specifying the purpose of the capital contribution, individual bank statements from each subscriber, signed subscription agreements, proof of the funding source (e.g., taxed employment savings, dividends, or asset liquidation statements), and a notarial confirmation of capital payment for the commercial register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business as a hobby-manufacturer and anticipated cross-border payment flow, including dense Asia-based supplier and distributor concentrations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed manufacturer-supplier agreements, purchase orders and pro-forma invoices, shipping and customs documentation (CMR, air waybills, customs declarations), licensing agreements for anime or mecha intellectual property, list of target import tariffs and HS codes, and a sanctions-screening policy showing counterparty screening of all payees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern about dual-use or military application of intellectual property due to 'mecha' or robotic terminology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product technical datasheets confirming non-functional, decorative plastic model-kit use; absence of controlled electronics, explosives, propulsion, or weapon components; legal opinion on Swiss goods-control classification (SECO or BAZG) classifying the kits as toy/hobby products; and end-user declarations from distributors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Swiss AG must be wired to the dedicated capital escrow account (Einzahlungskonto) in the name of the company at a Swiss bank before commercial-register registration. The preferred protocol is SWIFT MT103; the payment must cite the company name, subscriber name, and a clear reference such as 'Einzahlung Aktienkapital' (payment of share capital), together with the notarial deed number. Subscribers should transfer from their own bank accounts via their home-country correspondent to the Swiss beneficiary bank, and the corresponding transaction purpose must be a direct investment / equity participation, not a trade settlement. The Swiss bank will issue a blocking confirmation after the funds are credited and held for the statutory period subject to bank-internal lock protocols. Large direct-investment inflows in excess of SNB reporting thresholds must be reported on the relevant SNB balance-of-payments direct-investment form; all remitters and intermediaries must pass sanctions screening before credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for materials, tooling, and finished goods should be executed using SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for open-account transactions, documentary collections (DP/DA) where moderate trust exists, and commercial letters of credit (irrevocable, confirmed) via SWIFT MT700/MT707 for larger orders. For domestic CHF disbursements, the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system through the SNB provides final settlement. EUR payments to European suppliers may be routed via SEPA (TARGET2), and USD payments via CHIPS/Fedwire correspondents. All outbound messages must identify the commercial purpose using standard categories, the underlying invoice or contract number, and the ultimate beneficial counterparty where requested. PayPal is acceptable for low-value consumer refunds or smaller distributor pre-orders, but not for capital flows or material treasury operations. The company should maintain an annual cleared-payment matrix showing counterparty, sanctions-screening result, invoice, and customs documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards between CHF and EUR, USD, and JPY for firm purchase and sales exposures
FX swaps (swap and tomorrow-next rollover structures) for short-term liquidity management
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps to align the balance sheet with revenue and debt currency
Vanilla European FX options purchased for defined downside protection; uncovered option writing is not permitted for treasury-only purposes
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only when the counterparty currency is non-convertible and leg-currency deliverability is impossible; NDFs are not necessary or standard for CHF-based hedging
Currency futures via regulated exchanges, subject to the company's treasury risk policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and proposed profit appropriation submitted for shareholder approval; minutes of the ordinary shareholders' meeting and board discharge resolutions retained at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; presented to the shareholders' meeting and kept in the company's statutory records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end AG, no later than 30 June under Art. 699 para. 2 of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholders may petition the court to convene the meeting; directors face civil liability for non-compliance; persistent failure to convene may lead to judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual combined federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax and capital tax return, including financial statements, tax balance sheet, and computation of taxable equity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) of the canton of registered office, with the Federal Tax Administration receiving the federal direct tax share through the cantonal assessment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deadline is set by the canton, generally between 31 March and 30 September for a 31 December year-end; extension available on written request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 3.5% p.a.; late-filing penalty in practice up to CHF 10,000; default assessment after final deadline; criminal proceedings for deliberate tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and annual VAT reconciliation for the relevant VAT tax period, including input VAT deduction and output VAT on domestic and export sales.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT tax period; for a calendar-year period ending 31 December, normally due by 1 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a.; late-filing administrative fine in practice up to CHF 8,000; default VAT assessment; criminal penalties for false returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss withholding-tax self-declaration and payment for dividend distributions and other taxable profit benefits distributed to shareholders at the statutory withholding rate of 35%.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Withholding Tax Division.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the calendar month in which the taxable benefit was paid; no annual return is required for a non-distributing AG unless another taxable benefit is made.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate collection with default interest; administrative fine under the Swiss Withholding Tax Act; refund of withholding tax to shareholders may be denied if declaration is defective.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer's wage statement and social insurance settlement covering AHV/IV/EO, unemployment insurance ALV, pension fund BVG, and accident insurance UVG declarations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Fund (Ausgleichskasse) designated by the employer, with Suva or other licensed accident insurer for UVG matters.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage declaration and settlement for the previous calendar year generally due by 31 March of the following year in accordance with the compensation fund's instructions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, contribution surcharges, administrative fines for late or missing returns, and penal liability for willful failure to withhold or pay mandatory social contributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register audit and board confirmation covering the share register, board register, minute book, financial records, and supporting corporate resolutions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and company records at the Swiss registered office; no filing is made unless register facts trigger a Commercial Register amendment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the ordinary shareholders' meeting or, in any event, within the six-month statutory period for approving the annual financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate statutory records expose directors to civil liability and may constitute falsification of documents under Art. 251 of the Swiss Criminal Code; the court may order correction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner record review and, if triggered, any required notification to the Swiss transparency/beneficial-owner register regarding natural persons controlling the AG.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office or the central transparency register as designated by current federal law; internal UBO records also subject to review by banks and AML audits.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update promptly upon any ownership change; board review and annual attestation at the ordinary shareholders' meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate UBO documentation creates AML compliance failure; false declarations are subject to administrative fines and criminal liability for directors; persistent defaults may lead to registry intervention.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full ordinary audit is mandatory for a Swiss AG that exceeds two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 20 million; annual sales revenue above CHF 40 million; annual average of more than 250 full-time employees. Full audit is also required for listed companies and public-fundraising entities. A limited statutory audit applies to larger unlisted SMEs unless shareholders unanimously waive audit for a company with fewer than 10 full-time employees; shareholders holding at least 10% of share capital may demand a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting rules (Swiss GAAP, CO Art. 957-963) for the statutory individual financial statements; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Swiss GAAP FER may be applied for supplementary or group reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The board must annually review the natural persons who directly or indirectly hold or control more than 25% of the share capital or voting rights. Share register entries are updated immediately upon any transfer, and any mandatory beneficial-owner notification to the Swiss transparency register must be made within the period prescribed by current federal law. In the absence of a share transfer, no separate annual UBO filing is due; the annual review is recorded by board resolution.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managing Directors
Minute Book for shareholders' and board resolutions
Annual financial statements and audit or limited-review reports
Beneficial-owner documentation required under Swiss AML transparency provisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 3,500 per year depending on canton, domiciliation provider, and required administrative support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 12,000 per year for a non-listed manufacturing AG, depending on revenue, asset base, headcount, audit scope, and whether a full or limited audit is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct tax at 8.5% on post-tax net profit (approximately 7.83% on pre-tax profit), plus cantonal/municipal income tax; Zug effective combined rate approx. 14.6%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box relief (OECD Nexus-adjusted) reducing qualifying IP income by up to 90% at cantonal level; R&D super deduction up to 50% in most cantons; notional interest deduction on excess equity; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; tax-loss offset against future profits; combined incentives can bring effective rate to approx. 13–15% for qualifying manufacturing R&D activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss Federal/Cantonal Legal Entities Tax Return (Steuererklärung juristische Personen) filed via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's eTax Switzerland portal; in the Canton of Zug, the eTax-Zug / EFZ ePortal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; extended deadline generally up to 12 months after year-end upon formal application; tax period corresponds to the statutory financial year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, legal form, registered seat, Swiss UID and LexSeal number (if any).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Swiss AG, quote the Swiss company identification exactly as registered in the Commercial Register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates, opening and closing balance sheet dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Swiss Commercial Register financial statements; non-resident entities with a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) must file the Swiss PE's operating cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross assets on the closing balance sheet (balance sheet total).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss manufacturing AG, report all Swiss-located assets, including machinery and tooling used for injection molding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital and disclosed reserves (total shareholder equity).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent's equity contribution maintained in Switzerland should be shown as a shareholder loan or share premium, not as taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before tax (income statement under Swiss GAAP / full recognition).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the audited or approved Swiss statutory financial statements; foreign exchange adjustments must follow Swiss GAAP FER and be separately itemized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions to accounting profit: non-deductible expenses, hidden distributions, depreciation not accepted for tax, transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intercompany pricing adjustments from related parties outside Switzerland, including import raw materials and royalty charges, if arm's-length evidence is not timely provided.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions from accounting profit: tax-deductible provisions, participation relief, patent box deduction, R&D super-deduction, notional interest deduction and loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, dividend and royalty income from foreign sources may qualify for participation relief if a 10% shareholding or CHF 1 million acquisition cost exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income for federal and cantonal/municipal purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the federal rate of 8.5% on post-tax profit and the applicable Zug cantonal/municipal rate; deduct loss carryforwards up to 7 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal/municipal capital tax base (paid-in capital, reserves and retained earnings).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A manufacturing AG holding physical assets and employee payroll may be subject to capital tax on the Swiss equity stamped in the Canton of Zug.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reconciliation: declaration of dividends paid, qualifying treaty claims and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) certificate numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors claiming treaty relief must provide valid tax residency certificates (TRCs) and the FTA's exemption or refund authorization prior to distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 'Verspätungszuschlag' of up to 3% of the assessed tax and default interest of 4.5% per annum; administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 apply to negligent non-filing; intentional non-filing is prosecuted as tax evasion with penalties up to three times the evaded tax and possible imprisonment of directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss anticipatory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends paid by a Swiss AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must hold a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) in its home state. For a corporate shareholder owning at least 10% of the Swiss AG, Swiss law and most DTAs allow relief at source if the FTA has issued an advance ex-officio confirmation (Form 823E or USTS). If tax is withheld at 35%, the recipient must file a reclaim with the FTA within three years of the dividend payment date (generally under 3 years), attaching TRCs, corporate ownership evidence, and the paying agent's dividend voucher. Treaty rates range from 0% (participation exemption, e.g. EU/UK domestic threshold) to 15% for portfolio shareholdings; standard Swiss treaty rate for portfolio dividends is 15%, and for shareholdings of at least 10% generally 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Within Switzerland: royalties for IP use are not subject to Swiss withholding tax; interest on commercial loans, supplier credit and non-securitized debt is generally exempt from Swiss withholding tax. Swiss domestic withholding tax applies at 35% only to interest on Swiss corporate bonds, money-market instruments and bank deposits. Under Swiss DTAs, interest on ordinary intercompany loans is subject to treaty rates between 0% and 10% (frequently 0% in OECD-pattern DTAs); royalties are generally 0% to 10% depending on the IP character and the treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if the Swiss entity's gross related-party transactions (revenues plus expenses) exceed CHF 5 million in a tax year; Master File required if the group's annual consolidated revenue exceeds CHF 50 million; Country-by-Country report required file annually with the FTA when consolidated group revenue exceeds CHF 900 million. Below CHF 5 million, documentation does not need to be filed but should remain available upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the offshore sense; however, for treaty entitlement and for all tax privileges (participation relief, notional interest deduction, patent box), the Swiss AG must maintain real substance: employees, office/manufacturing premises, independent decision-making, and risk-taking functions in Switzerland. A 'letter-box' or conduit AG almost certainly triggers a denial of DTA benefits, retroactive withholding tax at 35% plus default interest, and potential penalties for abuse of tax law (Rechtsmissbrauch).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing false or incomplete income tax returns, concealing royalties from exported action-figure mecha kits, inflating intercompany costs, under-reporting Swiss-source income, or failing to disclose a Swiss permanent establishment of a foreign production entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of tax, default interest at 4.5%, and criminal penalty up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 175 DBG). If aggravated by forged documents, the offense is tax fraud under Art. 176 DBG with a fine of up to CHF 250,000 and up to 3 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve false tax returns are personally and jointly liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; they may be criminally punished with imprisonment up to 3 years, travel bans, and asset confiscation under Swiss criminal law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG with no commercial substance, no payroll, no Swiss manufacturing facility, no strategic control, and using it solely as a conduit to receive dividends, royalties, or interest from low-tax jurisdictions with the purpose of obtaining treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The FTA will deny the DTA claim, impose a 35% withholding tax on the entire pass-through amount (plus 4.5% default interest), and may re-characterize the distributions as hidden profit distributions subject to additional cantonal tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly create a sham Swiss entity can be personally assessed for the 35% unwithheld tax if the company is insolvent; they face criminal charges for participation in tax evasion, fines up to CHF 250,000, and a travel ban pending the criminal tax proceeding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany manufacturing margins, royalty expenses, or management fees materially below arm's length; failing to provide contemporaneous documentation despite the CHF 5 million threshold; using a Swiss AG as a low-profit contract manufacturer with no evidence of the arm's-length margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority re-determines the taxpayer's income under Art. 58 LIFD and Art. 24 LHID; imposes additional tax and default interest, and may levy a negligence penalty of up to 30% of the supplemental tax assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and transfer pricing coordinators are personally liable for the additional tax and penalty if they sign the statement certifying the intercompany transactions; in severe cases they are banned from serving as board members and may be imprisoned for 1 to 3 years for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to foreign shareholders without computing 35% Swiss withholding tax, or distributing profits under a false DTA certificate before the FTA grants relief at source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss AG is liable for the full 35% anticipatory tax (Art. 13 VStG), plus a late-payment penalty of up to 10% and 4.5% interest; unpaid withholding tax may be collected via enforced seizure of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing directors who instructed the unauthorized distribution become personally liable for the unpaid 35% and penalties; criminal prosecution for violation of the Swiss Withholding Tax Act can lead to a custodial sentence of up to 2 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Red Flag (Shell Manufacturing with Anonymous Payments)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving PayPal or wire transfer payments into the Swiss AG account for action-figure kits while the beneficial owner remains undisclosed, commingling private funds through the corporate account, or failing to record cash transactions above the reporting threshold for the purpose of tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the Swiss AG is used to conceal criminal assets, the offense is money laundering under Art. 305bis and 305ter of the Swiss Criminal Code: imprisonment up to 5 years, fines up to 500 day-units, asset freezing, and forfeiture of all proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in laundering funds through the AG face imprisonment from 3 to 5 years, a travel ban pending extradition, civil restitution to the Swiss state and injured shareholders, and disqualification from managing a company in Switzerland.
